title: A service bound to localhost is treated as unreachable and therefore unauthenticated, and the web tier proxies attacker parameters straight into it
index_line: T-0085 · FILE_WRITE · unauthenticated proxy to a no-auth localhost PostgreSQL sidecar: backupFile traversal → create/truncate any file · go · corroborated
invariant_violated: The sidecar assumed that binding to loopback made it unreachable by attackers, so it never implemented authentication; and the front end assumed its callers were the application. Both assumptions are false once the web tier exposes an endpoint that forwards caller-supplied parameters to the sidecar — 'only local processes can reach me' is not an access-control decision.

mechanism.does: an unauthenticated POST to the web tier's /v1/postgres/recovery/backup carries a database name and a caller-controlled backupFile
the web application proxies the request to the PostgreSQL sidecar listening on loopback, which performs no authentication at all
the sidecar joins backupFile onto its own service directory to form the dump destination
pg_dump is executed with that destination, so a ../../ backupFile creates or truncates any file the service account can write
the attacker chooses a destination the operating system consumes automatically — a cron entry, an authorized_keys file, a unit/service definition
the scheduler or service loader executes the planted content, turning an empty-file primitive into code execution

source.http.body.value: the JSON body of /v1/postgres/recovery/backup: database and backupFile, with no credentials required

sink.file.write.value: pg_dump writing to the path built from backupFile — file creation and truncation anywhere the service account can write

fs.path.join.value: the sidecar's join of its install directory with the caller's backupFile; ../../ resets out of the tree

guard.none.value: no authentication on the sidecar endpoint, no containment check on the destination path, and the proxy forwards without re-authorising

preconditions.expr: the Splunk web port answers and the sidecar proxy route exists (Splunk 10+ with the PostgreSQL sidecar enabled, default on AWS images)
the build is in the affected range (10.x below 10.0.7, 10.2.x below 10.2.4)

check.spec: curl -s http://HOST:8000/help 2>/dev/null | grep -oE 'Splunk [0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | head -1; splunk version 2>/dev/null | head -2

preconditions.expr: a PostgreSQL sidecar process is present and listening on loopback

success: a file appears at an attacker-chosen path outside the Splunk service directory
an existing file is truncated to zero length and its previous content is gone
failure_like: backupFile is reduced to a basename or the resolved path is checked against the service directory
false_positive: a 200 with a Pending/BackupPending state is the request being accepted, not proof of write — verify the file on disk
files created inside the service directory are normal backup behaviour

hazards: every appliance with an internal service mesh: sidecars, admin sockets, unix-domain APIs, and 'we only listen on 127.0.0.1' daemons
the front end is the authentication boundary only if it actually authorises every forwarded parameter
file creation alone is enough when a loader consumes the path (cron, systemd, authorized_keys, .pth, launchd)
non_transfers: sidecars that require a per-process secret or unix-socket permissions the web tier alone holds
proxies that validate parameters against an allowlist rather than forwarding them

evidence.target: Splunk Enterprise 10.x / 10.2.x, PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint (CVE-2026-20253)

provenance.author: watchTowr Labs
provenance.corroborates: CVE-2026-20253: the Splunk web tier proxies unauthenticated requests to the local PostgreSQL sidecar (/v1/postgres/recovery/backup); the endpoint has no authentication controls, and backupFile is joined onto the service directory, so ../../../ escapes it and pg_dump creates or truncates an arbitrary file

provenance.author: Splunk (SVD-2026-0603)
provenance.corroborates: vendor advisory: unauthenticated arbitrary file creation and truncation via a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint; the vulnerability exists because the endpoint lacks authentication controls, allowing any network-reachable user to invoke file operations without credentials
